 WP(C) NO. 21018 OF 2014  2  2025:KER:37109  JUDGMENT Petitioner raises claim for exemption from payment of building tax under Section 3(1)(b) of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.

According to the petitioner, the petitioner's establishment is a factory Kalyan Agro Foods vs The State Of Kerala on 27 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99526020/
1 and therefore, eligible for exemption.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The request was considered by the Government.

In order to verify whether the claim is sustainable and that whether the establishment of the petitioner would satisfy the definition of 'factory' under the Factories Act, Government issued Ext.P5 to the petitioner directing them to produce proof of registration under the Factories and Boilers Department as also of the muster roll for the past six months.
Petitioner produced Ext.P1 copy of the license and Ext.P4 series, extracts from the register of wages for different months.

After considering the request and materials produced by the petitioner, Government rejected the request vide Ext.P6 order dated 27.03.2014.
3.
It was observed by the Government in Ext.P6 that the establishment of the petitioner is an SSI Unit and that WP(C) NO. 21018 OF 2014 2025:KER:37109 5 persons are employed.

However, the request was rejected for the reason that only 5 persons are employed in the establishment and hence the establishment will not satisfy the requirement of the definition of the Factory under the Factories Act.

Factory is defined under the Factories Act as follows:
"Section 2(m) of the factories - 1948 reads as follows:
i) whereon ten or more workers are working, or were working on any day of the preceding twelve months, and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on with the aid of power, or is ordinarily so carried on, or ii) Whereon twenty or more workers are working, or were working on any day of the preceding twelve months, and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on without the aid of power, or is ordinarily so carried on, But does not include a mine subject to the operation of the Mines Act 1952 etc."
4 . Claim of the petitioner is that the establishment has employed total number of 12 workers including casual workers and permanent workers.
However, no document to show that 12 persons are actually engaged were produced before the Government.
Ext.P4 series of extracts of register of wages shows that 7 persons were being paid wages.
There is no convincing evidence to show that the petitioner's establishment has employed more than 10 WP(C) NO. 21018 OF 2014 2025:KER:37109 persons.
5. The learned Government Pleader relied on a judgment of this Court reported in [2025 KLT Online 1060] (Georgekutty P.J. v. State of Kerala).

entities.text: Georgekutty P.J. v. State of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgment, this Court upheld rejection of a claim for exemption for want of evidence in support of the claim.
6. As the petitioner has not substantiated the claim that more than 10 persons were engaged in his establishment, it cannot be said that Government has gone wrong in rejecting the claim.
Hence, I find no reason to interfere with Ext.P6.
This Writ Petition is accordingly dismissed.
